chapters.title: Control the Weather? No. Your Toga? Yes.
chapters.tease: Your weather app said zero percent, you are soaked, and a lame former slave from Nicopolis explains why that is fine.

chapters.title: The Senate Will Senate
chapters.tease: He ruled forty million people and could not make one room of senators behave. Here is how he stopped minding.

chapters.title: The Ox Has Opinions
chapters.tease: Forty minutes into the morning furrow, the ox sits down. No error message. Just an ox that has decided.

chapters.title: You Cannot Refresh the Past
chapters.tease: The Alexandrian mail fleet is sighted, the whole town runs to the docks, and Seneca stays exactly where he is.

chapters.title: Worry Is a Subscription You Can Cancel
chapters.tease: Your agent offers to do all your worrying as a managed service. Six hours later, it has produced exactly nothing.

chapters.title: The Omen Is Just Weather
chapters.tease: An admiral threw the sacred chickens into the sea, then lost ninety-three ships. Epictetus had a better way to read omens.

chapters.title: Delegate to the Gods (Everything Else Is Yours)
chapters.tease: A dog is tied to a moving cart. It can trot or be dragged. Either way, it arrives at the same place.

chapters.title: The Plague and the Panic
chapters.tease: The worst ticket in the empire's backlog could not be fixed. Marcus Aurelius worked it anyway, for fifteen years.

chapters.title: You Are Not Driving the Chariots
chapters.tease: Roman traffic was so bad Caesar banned carts by day. Epictetus solved road rage at the public baths.

chapters.title: Amor Fati: Love the Deployment
chapters.tease: Push a cylinder and it rolls. Push a cube and it just sits there. Chrysippus says you are the shape.

chapters.title: Wanting Less Is Getting More
chapters.tease: Seven courses, two wine services and a harpist for senators. Musonius Rufus reads the invitation and goes back to his bread.

chapters.title: The Hedonic Treadmill (Roman Model)
chapters.tease: Socrates walks through the market with his hands behind his back and leaves happier. His secret: how many things I don't need.

chapters.title: Negative Visualisation: The Free Upgrade
chapters.tease: The silk is perfect and the price is outrageous. Epictetus has a countdown timer, and it is set to twenty-four hours.

chapters.title: Enough Is a Number You Set
chapters.tease: January in Rome. The senator in gold trim is cold. The philosopher in a rough blanket is cold too, and happier.

chapters.title: The Tyranny of the Next Thing
chapters.tease: Rome built a perfect model of the hedonic treadmill out of wood, rope and men walking uphill to nowhere.

chapters.title: Diminishing Returns on the Second Cloak
chapters.tease: Forty-seven items on the wish list since February. The philosopher reads it once and deletes the lot. The agent produces confetti.

chapters.title: Compare and Despair
chapters.tease: Rome's richest private citizen sits in his vast wine cellar, drinking water and reading Epicurus. He sees no contradiction.

chapters.title: Hunger Is the Best Sauce
chapters.tease: A man at dinner quietly pictures his whole villa on fire. He opens his eyes, and the food tastes better.

chapters.title: The Cure for Craving Is Not More
chapters.tease: A man grieves loudly that there are no figs in winter. Epictetus tells him winter is not a defect.

chapters.title: Rich Is Having What You Need
chapters.tease: A man has hidden from his own shadow for three years. It has turned up every single morning anyway.

chapters.title: Anger Is Temporary Madness
chapters.tease: A short-changed merchant tries to count to ten in Roman numerals, gets lost at seven, and accidentally cures his rage.

chapters.title: The Pause Between Spark and Fire
chapters.tease: Someone slaps Cato the Younger in the public baths. When the man apologises, Cato says: I don't remember being hit.

chapters.title: No One Wrongs You on Purpose (Mostly)
chapters.tease: He writes the most devastating letter of his life, reads it once, and drops it into the fire. That was the point.

chapters.title: Count to Ten in Latin
chapters.tease: A volcano smokes behind him, and the philosopher stays calm, because pressure given time often just subsides.

chapters.title: The Insult Needs Your Signature
chapters.tease: Your agent fact-checks Seneca's three books on anger against two thousand years of science. The margin keeps saying: still true.

chapters.title: Revenge Runs Hot; Justice Runs Cool
chapters.tease: A small, decorated general lives in your head and wants to declare war over a slow waiter. Your agent intercepts the dispatch.

chapters.title: The Provocateur Wants a Reaction
chapters.tease: A man at the edge of the bath has spent minutes insulting the philosopher in it. Nothing lands. Here is why.

chapters.title: Sulking Is Anger in a Toga
chapters.tease: An orator is winning a furious argument with Marcus Aurelius, who is not there. The reply says seen, and nothing more.

chapters.title: The Grudge You Carry Weighs the Most
chapters.tease: He carries a torch to burn down his enemy's house. It is upside down, and it has been burning his own hand all week.

chapters.title: Cool the Passions, Keep the Fire
chapters.tease: The war room is screaming. Marcus Aurelius sits with his eyes closed, every slider at zero except one marked Reason.

chapters.title: The Obstacle Is the Way
chapters.tease: The road is blocked by rubble. Most travellers turn back. Marcus Aurelius steps onto it, because the rubble is the route.

chapters.title: The Shipwreck Founded a School
chapters.tease: Zeno lost his entire cargo of purple dye in a shipwreck, wandered into a bookshop, and walked out founding Stoicism.

chapters.title: Fire Tests Gold; Trouble Tests You
chapters.tease: Exiled to a rock on a trumped-up charge, Seneca sits down with a writing tablet. Status: thriving.

chapters.title: The Best Revenge Is a Good Build
chapters.tease: Two men cross the market. The strong one complains bitterly. The one with a crutch gets there faster, humming.

chapters.title: What Doesn't Bend, Breaks
chapters.tease: The general has twenty-four maps, labelled alpha to omega. He is fully committed to attacking at dawn, and fine with any of them.

chapters.title: Turn the Barrier into a Path
chapters.tease: The hill is steep, the amphora is full, and the man carrying it is smiling like an engineer running a load test.

chapters.title: The Difficult Is the Training
chapters.tease: Nothing is on fire. The family calmly files out of the villa anyway, says goodbye to it, and walks back in happier.

chapters.title: Fortune Favours the Prepared Mind
chapters.tease: Thrown twice and pinned once, the defeated wrestler skips the blaming and opens a notebook. The loss starts paying for itself.

chapters.title: Setbacks Are Data
chapters.tease: A man cheerfully signs a long contract called Fate. He has read Section 12, titled Everything. That is why he is smiling.

chapters.title: The Comeback Is Built in the Dark
chapters.tease: A cracked pot sits in Chrysippus' garden with a fig seedling thriving in the crack. The ticket is closed: working as designed.

chapters.title: Remember You Will Shut Down
chapters.tease: Every morning your agent sends one notification you cannot switch off: Reminder, mortal. Make it count. It is not morbid.

chapters.title: Time Is the Only Nonrenewable
chapters.tease: The scholar keeps a skull where you would put a second monitor. The agent benchmarked it: focus up, pointless meetings declined.

chapters.title: The Skull on the Desk
chapters.tease: Every account in the house can be topped up except one. It is the one everyone spends as if it were free.

chapters.title: You Could Leave Life Right Now
chapters.tease: Your agent tags everything in the garden with its sunset date: the statue, the villa, the roses, and finally, the owner.

chapters.title: Borrowed, Not Owned
chapters.tease: The one man who knows Rome will end gives the signal to raise the next marble column anyway. Plumb and true.

chapters.title: The Clock Was Always Running
chapters.tease: He is drafting his own eulogy and grinning, because the gap between the speech and his calendar is very useful.

chapters.title: Live as If the Rest Is Bonus
chapters.tease: A heroic marble statue is having its head unscrewed and replaced with this season's hero. Rome did this routinely.

chapters.title: What Would You Do with a Finished Life?
chapters.tease: At dusk a man watches his possessions float back toward the horizon. He is not being robbed. He is processing returns.

chapters.title: The Emperor and the Slave End the Same
chapters.tease: Yesterday's bread, olive oil and a little salt at dawn. The man eating it is clearly having a banquet.

chapters.title: Death: The Ultimate Log-Off
chapters.tease: Beneath an olive tree, at the end of a long life, an old man watches a ripe olive simply let go.

chapters.title: Virtue Is the Only KPI
chapters.tease: The emperor's dashboard once tracked forty-eight metrics. This morning it shows one gauge, labelled Virtue. The agent is hiding the rest.

chapters.title: Integrity Has No Dark Mode
chapters.tease: One man in the crowded forum and the same man alone in a midnight alley. The agent searched for a second configuration. There isn't one.

chapters.title: The Four Virtues, One Dashboard
chapters.tease: Behind the virtue gauge are four stone dials, worn smooth by centuries of hands. Turn any one and the others move.

chapters.title: Wisdom: Read the Docs
chapters.tease: Cleanthes hauled water all night so he could study all day, writing lectures on ox shoulder-blades. His nickname was the Ass.

chapters.title: Courage Without an Audience
chapters.tease: An off-duty soldier helps a fallen stranger on an empty street at night. No crowd, no medal, camera firmly off.

chapters.title: Justice Isn't a Feature Flag
chapters.tease: A senator in gold and a beggar in rags stand before the magistrate. Identical weights, identical scales. No premium tier.

chapters.title: Temperance and the Second Amphora
chapters.tease: The wine is excellent and the host insists. A guest quietly covers his cup with his palm. The first cup was for thirst.

chapters.title: Be the Rock the Waves Hit
chapters.tease: The sea hurls itself at a rocky headland. Marcus Aurelius wrote this image about himself, and the sea always loses.

chapters.title: Reputation Is Read-Only
chapters.tease: There is unflattering graffiti about him on the wall. He sees it and keeps walking, because he never had write access.

chapters.title: Character: Compiles Daily
chapters.tease: A sculptor carves a statue of himself, a little every day. Tonight's build, number twelve thousand seven hundred and seventy-five, passes.

chapters.title: The Cosmopolis Group Chat
chapters.tease: You were added to one enormous group chat at birth. Members: everyone. Leave group: disabled. The Stoics invented it.

chapters.title: People Will Be People (It's in the Spec)
chapters.tease: Today's forecast: humans, one hundred percent. Marcus Aurelius read it every morning, and dressed accordingly.

chapters.title: Forgive Like a Server: 200 OK
chapters.tease: He was badly wronged, and everyone expected a feud. Instead he returned peace, and saved no copy of the grievance.

chapters.title: The Difficult Colleague Simulator
chapters.tease: In the gym, a philosopher lifts a bronze statue of his most annoying colleague, mid-eye-roll. Excellent workout.

chapters.title: Sympathy Without Sync Issues
chapters.tease: A woman shakes with grief. Her friend holds her, fully moved, and does not shake. That steadiness is the gift.

chapters.title: Teaching Without Tweeting
chapters.tease: A goat lectures nobody about its grazing. A sheep says nothing and grows magnificent wool. Epictetus knew which to be.

chapters.title: The Banquet Seating Problem
chapters.tease: A platter circles the banquet table. One diner lunges across two neighbours. Our guest waits with his hands in his lap.

chapters.title: Praise Is Spam
chapters.tease: A courtier bows low and floats exquisite compliments at the philosopher. The agent stamps every one: suspicious link, do not click.

chapters.title: Crowds: High Latency, Low Signal
chapters.tease: Seneca went to the games for light entertainment and came home more cruel and inhuman. So he started choosing his inputs.

chapters.title: Friendship: The Original Peer Network
chapters.tease: After all the warnings about crowds and flatterers, the Stoics land somewhere warm: two old friends, laughing at half a sentence.

chapters.title: Rich Stoic, Poor Stoic
chapters.tease: Seneca's marble villa and Epictetus's hut with one lamp. Two very different inventories. The inner readings are identical.

chapters.title: The Villa Is Not the Vibe
chapters.tease: He moved to a cliffside villa with a perfect sea view to be happy. His unhappiness came too, and took the good chair.

chapters.title: Fame: A Trend That Forgets You
chapters.tease: A man sprints after a laurel wreath tumbling down an endless road. The wreath, being wind, keeps moving.

chapters.title: Diogenes' Minimalist Setup
chapters.tease: Alexander the Great offers Diogenes anything he wants. Diogenes asks him to stand out of the sunlight.

chapters.title: The Purple Robe Subscription
chapters.tease: A senator is drowning in yards of purple robe, each chain link a receipt. He signed up for status and never read the recurring terms.

chapters.title: Net Worth vs. Self Worth: Different Ledgers
chapters.tease: An accountant keeps two scrolls. One lurches with every grain rumour. The other is a flat, steady line. Guess which one is you.

chapters.title: Laurel Wreath Inflation
chapters.tease: A market stall sells laurel wreaths, three for the price of one. Everyone is crowned, so the crown means nothing.

chapters.title: The Triumph Parade and the Whisper
chapters.tease: At the peak of a Roman triumph, with the whole city roaring, a voice in the general's ear says: remember, you are mortal.

chapters.title: Gold Is Heavy; Travel Light
chapters.tease: Two men in the water after a shipwreck. One swims easily to shore. The other will not let go of his chest of gold.

chapters.title: Own Things That Don't Own You Back
chapters.tease: A man stands before his magnificent villa on a leash. The surprise is which way it runs: the house holds the other end.

chapters.title: The Morning Standup with Yourself
chapters.tease: Every morning Marcus Aurelius held a standup meeting with one attendee and a brief with exactly one item: be good.

chapters.title: Journaling: Meditations Was a Private Repo
chapters.tease: The most-read philosophy book in the world was written by a man who never wanted a single reader.

chapters.title: Cold Plunge, Hot Take
chapters.tease: Seneca lowers himself into a freezing bath in January and lets out a controlled, senatorial shriek. On purpose.

chapters.title: Voluntary Discomfort Sprints
chapters.tease: There is a perfectly good bed right there. Its owner is sleeping on the floor beside it, by choice. He is doing a rep.

chapters.title: The Evening Retro
chapters.tease: By candlelight, Seneca reviews his whole day in three columns: well, poorly, tomorrow. There is no blame column.

chapters.title: Premeditatio Malorum: The Daily Backup
chapters.tease: At dawn, your agent renders thumbnails of the day's possible disasters: spilled wine, a lost ship, a rude senator. Surprises remaining: zero.

chapters.title: Fasting: Scheduled Downtime
chapters.tease: A great feast is in full swing, and a philosopher walks cheerfully past it to a simple bowl, on purpose.

chapters.title: Walk It Off, Peripatetically
chapters.tease: The problem would not yield at the desk. Somewhere around the second mile of walking, it started coming apart on its own.

chapters.title: The Discipline of Assent
chapters.tease: A thought knocks, dressed as fact: this is a disaster. The philosopher keeps the door on the chain and asks for credentials.

chapters.title: Repetition Until Character
chapters.tease: A target with a thousand arrows packed into its centre. The archer no longer has to aim. He just practised.

chapters.title: Zoom Out Until Rome Is a Pixel
chapters.tease: Marcus Aurelius rises in his mind until Rome is a pixel. At ten thousand times zoom, your problem is not visible.

chapters.title: You Are a Limb of the Whole
chapters.tease: Many separate figures across a landscape. The agent draws glowing lines between them, and they turn out to be one body.

chapters.title: The Cosmos Doesn't Take Requests
chapters.tease: A man stands in a field at night shouting demands at the stars. The universe closes his ticket: works as intended.

chapters.title: Star Stuff with Sandals
chapters.tease: A philosopher's silhouette is filled with stars. He is made of the same fire as the constellations, and invited to act like it.

chapters.title: Eternal Recurrence, Beta
chapters.tease: The Stoics believed the universe burns down and reboots from the same seed, so your exact life airs again. Would you greenlight it?

chapters.title: The Logos: Original Source Code
chapters.tease: A river made not of water but of readable logic flows past Chrysippus. The source code of reality was open all along.

chapters.title: Everything Is Connected (Mostly via Aqueducts)
chapters.tease: A single dropped coin sets off a cascade across a Roman city and waters a garden three streets away.

chapters.title: A Festival, Briefly Attended
chapters.tease: The festival is ending at dusk. A man leaves, turns back and waves. Five stars. Would live again.

chapters.title: The Long Now of Marcus
chapters.tease: Between the ruins of the past and the unbuilt future, Marcus holds one point of warm light. It is all anyone ever has.

chapters.title: Log Off Gracefully: The Stoic Exit
chapters.tease: The door in the quiet room was always open. That, said Epictetus, is exactly why you can stay calmly in it.
